Where it began

Andrew Flintoff was born in Preston, Lancashire, on 6 December 1977, into a cricketing house. His father, Colin, captained the Dutton Forshaw second XI, and his brother Chris played the game too. At school a surname close to Fred Flintstone's earned him the name Freddie.

He came through the Lancashire Schools sides at under-11 and under-15 level, left school at 16, and played for England's under-19 side for two and a half years, captaining it on their tour of Pakistan in 1996/7.

The player

His Test debut came against South Africa at Trent Bridge in 1998. The early years were patchy, but a new bowling action took him to India in 2001–02, and his first Test hundred followed against New Zealand in 2002. In 2004 he made 167 against the West Indies at Edgbaston and was named a Wisden Cricketer of the Year.

Then came 2005. At Edgbaston he hit more sixes than Ian Botham had ever managed in an Ashes Test, took seven wickets, including Justin Langer and Ricky Ponting in a single over, and England won by two runs. Michael Vaughan called it Fred's Test. He made a hundred at Trent Bridge, took five wickets on the fourth day at The Oval, and was Man of the Series as the Ashes came home. In all he played 79 Tests from 1998 to 2009, making 3,845 runs at 31.78 with five hundreds and 26 fifties, and taking 226 wickets at 32.79, with a best of 5 for 58.

What made him special

He gave a side three players in one: a fast bowler who could make good batsmen hop, a batsman who could take a game away in an hour, and a fine slip fielder who held 51 Test catches. Asked to lead England in India in 2006, he did it with bat and ball, won by 212 runs in Mumbai and was player of the series. His last Test summer, in 2009, brought five wickets at Lord's and a run-out of Ponting at The Oval as England won the series 2–1.

If there was a gap, it was in the hundreds column. For a man who struck the ball so cleanly, five Test centuries feels a modest return.

Away from the middle

The honours piled up in 2005 and 2006: the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy, shared with Jacques Kallis, BBC Sports Personality of the Year, an MBE and the Freedom of Preston. After cricket he found a second career on screen. He captained a team on A League of Their Own, was crowned King of the Jungle when Australia first staged I'm a Celebrity, in 2015. He went on to coach the England Lions from 2024 to August 2026, and was named senior coach of the Sydney Thunder for the 2026-27 season.

And finally

During that 167 at Edgbaston in 2004, with 20,000 watching, Flintoff launched one six high into the Ryder Stand. A spectator rose to take the catch and put it down. It was his father. Colin, it seems, was a cricketer first and a fielder second.
